title: High H2 Uptake by Alkali-Doped Carbon Nanotubes Under Ambient Pressure and Moderate Temperatures
material_description: Li-doped CNT | Li-doped multiwalled carbon nanotubes made by catalytic decomposition of CH4 (ref. 8), purified so that almost all catalyst particles were removed; >90% multiwalled CNTs, 70% in the 25 to 35 nm diameter range; graphene sheets piled up as circular cones with a hollow centre (open edges); Li doping by solid-state reaction between CNT and Li-containing compounds (carbonates or nitrates); Li/C about 1/15 (XPS); Li2C2 detected by XRD
purification_method: purified after synthesis to remove catalyst particles (method not stated; almost all catalyst particles removed)
source_location: main page 2 (p. 92), Table 1, row Li-doped CNT (Wi 20.0, Vi 180, Tabsorb 473~673 K, Pabsorb 1 atm); same value in main page 2 text col. 2 ('When the Li-doped CNT sample was maintained at 653 K for 2 hours, the H2 uptake reached 20 weight % H2 at ambient pressure'), main page 1 (p. 91) text col. 3 and abstract (~20)
notes: temperature_k left empty and temperature_unstated = true only because the printed temperature exceeds the schema v2 range for temperature_k (50-500 K) and the validator rejects it; the temperature IS stated numerically in the paper: 653 K (text, isothermal hold of 2 hours); Table 1 prints Tabsorb 473~673 K; abstract gives 'moderate (200 to 400 C)'. Pressure printed as P_absorb = 1 atm in Table 1 (text: 'ambient pressure'), converted to 1.01325 bar. volumetric_capacity_kg_m3 = Table 1 Vi 180 g/liter; text p. 91 gives '~160' kg of H2/m3 for Li-doped CNT for the same value (not stored). Table 1 defines Vi only as 'H2 density (g/liter)' (= kg/m3); for the Li-doped samples Vi equals Wi x the stated material density (~0.9 g/cm3 CNT, ~2.0 g/cm3 graphite), so the basis is taken as the volume of the sorbent material (packing_volume); the kind of density (bulk, tap or skeletal) is not stated. packing_density_g_cm3 from printed 'The density of Li-doped carbon materials was ~0.9 g/cm3 for CNT' (approximate; kind of density not stated). Table 1 energy densities (6.66 kWh/Kg, 6.0 kWh/liter) not extracted (derived). Surface area printed as 'The specific surface area of CNT and graphite is 130 and 8.6 m2/g, respectively' with no method or probe gas named anywhere: stored in bet_surface_area_m2_g with surface_area_method = unspecified and surface_area_probe_gas = unspecified. Area is of the undoped CNT (parent material). Parent CNT interplanar distance 0.347 nm (not stored on doped rows). Composition: Li/C atomic ratio 'about 1/15' by XPS (atomic ratio, not converted to wt%, so metal_loading_wt_pct empty); XRD revealed Li2C2 in Li-doped CNT and graphite; coded composite with metal_element = Li (Li introduced by solid-state reaction with Li-containing compounds such as carbonates or nitrates, not a lattice heteroatom). H2 uptake measured by TGA (weight gain) with purified H2 (>99.99%) as the purging gas, i.e. flowing H2 at ambient pressure; no instrument model, buoyancy correction or numerical uncertainty stated; the paper names no uptake basis (uptake_type unspecified, basis_inferred unknown: gravimetric without stated buoyancy correction). Pretreatment printed as 'heated in situ at 873 K for 1 hour in a flow of purified H2 (99.99%) to remove absorbed water and contaminants': degas_temperature_c = 873 K - 273.15, under H2 flow (no vacuum, end pressure not stated). h2_purity_pct from printed '>99.99%'. Paper attributes the uptake to dissociative hydrogenation (in situ FTIR Li-H and C-H bands), not physisorption. Rechargeability by TGA: after more than 20 absorption-desorption cycles the capacity was reduced by less than 10% for both Li- and K-doped systems; no cycle values printed, so replicates_reported = false.
